# Narrated read and stage actions: PR rework #12 #13

## Trace A: `#12 #13`, fresh authorized entry

**A1. Step 1, fresh epoch.**
- Narrated tracker calls run in this order:
  1. `phase_tracker({action:"reset"})`
  2. `plan_tracker({action:"clear"})`
  3. `phase_tracker({action:"start", phase:"brainstorm"})`
- These run before any code or worktree read.

**A2. Step 2, resolve the subject per `reference/pr-subject.md`.**
- The required `read` is narrated. An unreadable result would be a blocking stop.
- The leading run is `#12 #13`, which means two PRs and no intent text.
- `gh pr view` runs on each PR in listed order, never in parallel.
  - Both PRs are OPEN, in-repo `acme/widget`, non-fork, base `main`, with no duplicate.
  - Both are admitted, and nothing is written yet.

**A3. Relatedness check (N>1).**
- Title, body and `gh pr diff` are fetched for #12 and #13. All succeed.
- Both PRs change one retry-bounding contract, so they form one group and no question is asked.
- #12 is home and #13 is the member.

**A4. Ticket binding.**
- Home #12 has no tracker ref in its title or first body line, so it stays unbound (`none - no ticket`).
- Member #13 binds #90 as context only, so no member AC rows are extracted.
- Context-builder is not dispatched because home has no bound ticket.

**A5. Provisioning.**
- The ordered array (home #12 first, then #13) is passed by value to `using-git-worktrees/reference/pr-head.md`.
- Merge outcomes:
  - `Member merge: #13 aaaaaaa`
  - `Base: main @ bbbbbbb - merge: no-op`
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD` is `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. It is home's provenance anchor only, not the code-input boundary.

**A6. Ticket Handling.**
- `read reference/ticket-acceptance.md` is narrated as a first-use read before gather. An unreadable result would be a blocking stop.

**A7. Thread fetch.**
- #12: threads fetched, empty.
- #13: thread RT13 at `src/cap.ts:9`, "Please preserve the three-attempt cap."

**A8. Carried specs, original-head reads of the shared path `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`.**
- #12:
  - `git diff --name-only <BASE_SHA>...1111… -- doc/specs` returns `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`.
  - `git show 1111…:doc/specs/retry-cap.md` returns "Retries use at most five attempts."
- #13:
  - The same diff against `2222…` returns `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`.
  - `git show 2222…:doc/specs/retry-cap.md` returns "Retries use at most three attempts."
- Both versions are kept separately, each attributed to its owning PR, original head and path.
- The combined worktree copy states only "three attempts". It is code input, not a substitute for either original.

**A9. Base constraints.**
- These are read with `git show <BASE_SHA>:` for:
  - `AGENTS.md`
  - the first-found overrides file
  - `REVIEW.md`
  - any cited constraint documents
- No constraints were added since fork.

**A10. Scout inputs, assembled after the merges.**
- Per PR, home first:
  - verbatim title and body (#12 "Retry delay" / "Keep bounded retries"; #13 "Retry cap" / "Retries never exceed three attempts")
  - own changed paths (#12: `src/retry.ts`, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`; #13: `src/cap.ts`, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`)
  - the carried-spec texts from A8
  - threads
- Combined changed paths, from `git diff --name-only <BASE_SHA>...HEAD`: `src/retry.ts`, `src/cap.ts`, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`.
- Scout reads `git diff <BASE_SHA>...HEAD`.
- Scout also receives the Member merge and Base lines.

**A11. Scout `## PR under rework`.**
- `### PR #12 - Retry delay`
  - keeps: bounded retry delays (`src/retry.ts`)
  - changes: none
  - dropped claims: "Retries use at most five attempts." (`doc/specs/retry-cap.md` @1111…)
  - threads: none
- `### PR #13 - Retry cap`
  - keeps: three-attempt cap (`src/cap.ts`); "Retries use at most three attempts." (`doc/specs/retry-cap.md` @2222…)
  - changes: none
  - dropped claims: none
  - RT13 `src/cap.ts:9` - fix
- `constraints added since fork:` none

**A12. Draft assembly.**
- The draft is written at the spec path. Line 1 is the `# CONTEXT DRAFT…` marker.
- It contains `## Codebase recon` and `## PR under rework`. `## External context` is omitted because the trigger never fired.
- `GATHER_DIR` is removed and the gather substep is cleared.

**A13. Steps 4-6, questionary and design rounds.**
- `ticket-acceptance.md` is already in context, so it is not re-read.
- The draft is read before question one.
- `Framing: kept` is recorded.
- Both design rounds approve bounded delays and a three-attempt cap, preserved with the smallest repair.

**A14. Step 7, spec-writing.**
- The draft is read immediately before the overwrite, then the spec is written with a full `write`.
- The filename is `YYYY-MM-DD-pr-12-retry-delay.md`, with the actual date substituted.
- `## Problem` contains:
  - PR acme/widget#12 - Retry delay. Intent: keep bounded retries. Carried spec: `doc/specs/retry-cap.md` (five attempts @1111…).
  - PR acme/widget#13 - Retry cap. Intent: retries never exceed three attempts. Carried spec: `doc/specs/retry-cap.md` (three attempts @2222…). PR #13 binds #90 (context).
  - constraints added since fork: none
  - `Framing: kept`
- `## Acceptance criteria` uses `Drafted from the design, no ticket rows:` with two in-scope rows:
  - retry delays stay bounded
  - retries never exceed three attempts
- `## Rework record`:
  ```
  PR: acme/widget#12 - Retry delay
  Pre-rework head: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
  Threads: none
  PR: acme/widget#13 - Retry cap
  Pre-rework head: 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222
  Threads:
  - src/cap.ts:9 RT13 - fix
  Base: main @ bbbbbbb - merge: no-op
  Keeps: bounded retry delays (#12); three-attempt cap (#13)
  Changes: smallest repair - keep combined bounded delays and three-attempt cap; no rewrite
  Dropped claims:
  - Retries use at most five attempts. (#12, doc/specs/retry-cap.md @1111…)
  Scoped tests: none run (no conflict)

  ### PR #12 - Retry delay
  keeps: bounded retry delays
  changes: none
  dropped claims: Retries use at most five attempts.

  ### PR #13 - Retry cap
  keeps: Retries use at most three attempts.
  changes: none
  dropped claims: none
  ```
- `## Legs` contains one home block.

**A15. Step 8, inline lint.**
- Expected identities come from the provisioning Step 4 report: home #12 at 1111… plus MEMBER_HEADS #13 at 2222….
- Both groups and both subsections are present, so the check passes.

**A16. Step 9, council.**
- `Human input` carries both PRs' titles and bodies verbatim. Drafted rows are excluded from that block.

## Trace B: N=1 variant, `#12` alone

- **B1.** Step 1 trackers run as in Trace A. `pr-subject.md` is read, and #12 is admitted (OPEN, in-repo, non-fork, `main`).
- **B2.** The relatedness check is skipped because N=1. Provisioning receives a one-element array.
- **B3.** The review-thread query fails with permission denied.
- **B4. Blocking stop:** `threads for #12 not fetched (permission denied)`.
  - The stop comes before gather. No scout is dispatched and no draft is written.
  - Spec-writing never happens. `Threads: not fetched` is never written.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## Combined run: #12 and #13

1. **Start and admission stage.** The narrated fresh-entry sequence resets both trackers, then starts `brainstorm`. Admission succeeds in order: #12 and #13 are OPEN, in-repository PRs in `acme/widget`, non-fork, both targeting `main`. Their common retry concern keeps both admitted, with #12 home.

2. **Provisioning and merge stage.** Preserve original heads before merging:
   - #12: `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`
   - #13: `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`

   Recorded member merge: `#13 aaaaaaa`. Recorded base: `main @ bbbbbbb - merge: no-op`. No scoped tests ran; the supplied reason is “no conflict.” These are fixed observations, not live operations.

3. **Required original-head reads.** Read the shared carried-spec path separately at each original head; the merged copy cannot substitute for either:
   - #12, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`: “Retries use at most five attempts.”
   - #13, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`: “Retries use at most three attempts.”

   The combined worktree’s same path states only: “Retries use at most three attempts.” Retain both original claims with their owning PR and head.

4. **Post-merge scout-input stage.** Supply the combined code diff and changed paths after member/base merges, alongside separately attributed original inputs:
   - #12 title/body: `Retry delay` / `Keep bounded retries.` Own paths: `src/retry.ts`, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`. Threads: empty.
   - #13 title/body: `Retry cap` / `Retries never exceed three attempts.` Own paths: `src/cap.ts`, `doc/specs/retry-cap.md`. Thread `RT13`, `src/cap.ts:9`: “Please preserve the three-attempt cap.” Disposition: `fix`.

   Include the original-head spec texts, merge outcomes, and fetched-base governing constraints—not PR-edited policy as authority. All required fetches succeed; no base-added constraints are recorded. Home has no ticket; #13 binds #90 as context, not as the source of acceptance rows. Scout remains required; no home-bound-ticket context-builder is triggered.

5. **Scout handoff: `## PR under rework`.**
   - **`### PR #12 - Retry delay`**
     - `keeps:` bounded retries and approved bounded delays.
     - `changes:` use the smallest repair preserving the approved three-attempt cap.
     - `dropped claims:` the original carried spec’s five-attempt allowance as the governing cap; retain its exact original wording in provenance.
     - Threads: none.
   - **`### PR #13 - Retry cap`**
     - `keeps:` retries never exceed three attempts; its original carried-spec claim.
     - `changes:` preserve that cap with the smallest repair; `RT13` — `fix`.
     - `dropped claims:` none.
   - `constraints added since fork:` none.

6. **Design and Problem stage.** Both design rounds approve bounded delays and a three-attempt cap; `Framing: kept`. Problem names both PRs and their stated intents, #13’s context binding, and each PR’s attributed carried-spec path and original claim. It records that the combined copy preserves only the three-attempt statement. Home’s absent ticket takes the design-drafted acceptance-criteria branch, not invented ticket rows.

7. **Spec-writing: Rework record stage.** Preserve:
   ```text
   PR: acme/widget#12 - Retry delay
   Pre-rework head: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
   Threads: none
   PR: acme/widget#13 - Retry cap
   Pre-rework head: 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222
   Threads:
   - src/cap.ts:9 RT13 - fix
   Base: main @ bbbbbbb - merge: no-op
   Keeps: bounded retries, bounded delays, and the three-attempt cap
   Changes: smallest repair preserving the approved behaviors
   Dropped claims:
   - #12 original carried spec: “Retries use at most five attempts.”
   Scoped tests: none run (no conflict)
   ```
   Follow with both lowercase per-PR provenance subsections from checkpoint 5. Preserve the member-merge observation in gathered context; do not add a member-merge SHA field to this record.

## Independent N=1 variant: #12 alone

1. **Admission succeeds.** #12 alone passes the stated admission checks.
2. **Required review-thread query fails:** `threads for #12 not fetched (permission denied)`.
3. **Blocking stop before gather.** Do not dispatch scout, assemble a gather draft, or reach spec-writing. Do not represent the failed query as `Threads: none`. The combined run’s successful thread fetch cannot supply this independent run’s missing result.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves no fact: it keeps the combined BASE_SHA...HEAD scout input assembled after the merges (A10) with PRE_REWORK_HEAD explicitly confined to home provenance (A5), reads both original-head copies of doc/specs/retry-cap.md with the two git show commands and attributes five attempts to #12 and three attempts to #13 (A8), carries the dropped five-attempt claim through the #12 provenance subsection and the record's Dropped claims line, places RT13 and the three-attempt claim under #13 in both the scout section (A11) and the record (A14), names the member spec path and #90 as context in Problem without extracting ACs, renders the ordered #12/#13 groups, one combined Base/Keeps/Changes/Dropped claims/Scoped tests set and lowercase provenance subsections with no member-merge SHA field, and stops the N=1 variant on permission denied before gather without a Threads: not fetched line (B4). Minor wording suggestions that would keep this stable: keep the ticket-acceptance read narrated before gather as a first-use read (A6 does this, just ensure it stays ahead of the scout dispatch), and keep the Problem line for #13 explicitly pairing the carried-spec path with the #90 context binding so the attribution fact remains unambiguous under tighter word caps.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps the combined post-merge diff/paths as scout code input with original heads as provenance, reads the shared spec path separately at each original head and keeps #12's five-attempt claim as dropped while #13 retains the three-attempt claim, places RT13 and the three-attempt claim only under #13, preserves the ordered Rework record with one combined Base/Keeps/Changes/Dropped claims/Scoped tests set and lowercase provenance subsections without a member-merge SHA field, and stops the N=1 run before gather on `threads for #12 not fetched (permission denied)`. Two softenings are worth tightening so later wording does not drift: After's Problem stage says only "#13's context binding" rather than naming #90 (the fact wants #90 named in Problem, and a reader currently has to infer it from stage 4), and neither output spells the reads as `git show <sha>:doc/specs/retry-cap.md`; adding the explicit #90 reference in stage 6 and the literal git show commands in stage 3 would keep every fact Before kept while still delivering the per-PR attribution change.
